newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-BLEDSOE ON WHIRLWIND RIDE TO SUPER BOWL.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-BLEDSOE ON WHIRLWIND RIDE TO SUPER BOWL.

text.p: Before being selected first overall in the 1993 NFL draft, Drew Bledsoe remembers marvelling at Dallas qaurterback Troy Aikman making it to the Super Bowl in just his fourth year in the National Football League.
On Tuesday it dawned on the young New England Patriots signal caller that he has accomplished the very same thing.

"I remember thinking wouldn't that be great to come into the NFL and in four years be in the Super Bowl, that was kind of the ultimate dream -- can we get there as quickly as the Cowboys? And here we are four years after the draft and I'm in the Super Bowl.
"So it's been a real whirlwind ride," said the 24-year-old quarterback, who on Sunday faces the daunting task of taking on the heavily-favoured Green Bay Packers in Super Bowl XXXI.
"It's starting to set in now that we're actually in the Super Bowl. It's all happened extremely quickly.
"You say it's just a game but it's the ultimate stage for the ultimate game."

The enormously talented quarterback seemed somewhat less prepared for his first Super Bowl media day, during which hordes of reporters, broadcasters, cameramen and photographers descend en masse to swarm players on the field like no rush Bledsoe has ever faced from opposition defences.
"This whole thing is kind of surreal. It's part of the game that wasn't part of the dream when I was growing up," he admitted.
"I always dreamed about being on the field but all this stuff is new."

Green Bay's great defensive end Reggie White, who will be coming at Bledsoe Sunday with the same ferocity as some of the cameramen did Tuesday, acknowledged that the New England quarterback can be forced into errors at this early juncture of his career. But he also paid tribute of his youthful foe.
"If you get consistent pressure on him, you can make him make mistakes," White said of Bledsoe.

"One thing that you've got to give him is his kudos," added the Green Bay sackmaster. "He's done a good enough job to get his team this far and that means that he's one of the quarterbacks to be reckoned with in this league."
Bledsoe said his teammates seem to be feeding off being tagged as 14-point underdogs.
"This team has been very good at using the underdog role or the lack of respect as a motivator," he said.
Bledsoe even provided an anecdote to demonstrate his team's second class status here.

He said a man approached him at a restaurant Monday night and asked if he played for the Packers. When informed that Bledsoe played for the other team, the fellow apparenly could not name the Packers' Super Bowl opponent.
"We're the anonymous guys down here," Bledsoe said.
"I think that this team has accomplished more than people gave us a chance to at the beginning of the year and we're proud of that fact.
"But if we don't win this game we'll be remembered as a team that ... came up short."
And while thrilled to have reached the big show so swiftly, Bledsoe knows he has one more hurdle before he can take his place alongside Aikman.

"Until you win this game as a quarterback you always have something to prove. And even then you have to come back the next year and you've got to prove it again," he said, displaying some of the wisdom in the ways of the world he has acquired along the way.

Bledsoe also insisted that his team cannot and will not be adversely affected by the widely reported rumours that head coach Bill Parcells will leave the team after the Super Bowl due to a rift with Patriots owner Robert Kraft.
"We've heard all this stuff about Bill," he said.
"It started last year and at this point nothing is going to break this team's concentration unless there was a nuclear war."
